summary: Test present elements in ascending order until a callback result becomes truthy, skipping holes.

target.notes: Snapshot length; for each present index invoke callback via JsFunction.Call, apply JsValue.IsTruthy, and return true immediately on the first truthy result. Skip absent indices.

semantics.callback_callable_check: TypeError before iteration if callback is not callable

caveats: A direct Enumerable.Any is only safe under stronger representation/callback assumptions than this general array rule.
Callback-return objects are truthy even when empty; do not require a C# bool return type.

tests.name: skips holes and short-circuits
tests.input: const seen=[]; const r=[,1,2,3].some((v,i)=>{seen.push(i); return v===2}); console.log(r,seen.join(','));

tests.name: appended values beyond initial length are ignored
